items.entity: design domain orientation (40-by-120 mesh)
items.description: Sec. 5.2 only says 'a 2D structure represented by a 40-by-120 mesh, see Fig. 1a' (N = 4800 in Sec. 3.2). It does not say which count runs along the beam axis and which through the depth, or how the cantilever is oriented. Only Fig. 1a, which is not available, shows this.
readings: 120 elements along the beam axis (horizontal) x 40 elements deep: 3:1 horizontal cantilever, support on a 40-element edge, load at the mid-node of the opposite 40-element edge
40 elements along the beam axis x 120 elements deep: 1:3 deep cantilever, support on a 120-element edge
vertical cantilever 40 wide x 120 tall, support on the bottom edge, load at the mid-node of the top edge (reading 1 rotated 90 deg; matters if load angles are measured in global axes)

items.entity: element size / physical dimensions of the domain
items.description: Only element counts are given. No physical length, height, element size or element aspect ratio is stated anywhere (the structured grid implies square elements).
readings: unit square elements, domain 120 x 40 length units
square elements of size 1/40, domain 3 x 1
square elements of size 1/120, domain 1 x 1/3

items.entity: finite-element formulation
items.description: Sec. 3.2 only says K is assembled from the densities rho for a linear-elastic, small-displacement 2D structure. Element type and integration scheme are not stated.
readings: 4-node bilinear quadrilateral (Q4), full 2x2 Gauss integration (88-line-code style)
Q4 with incompatible modes or reduced integration

items.entity: fixed end of the cantilever
items.description: Only the Fig. 1 caption ('cantilever beam', load 'at the tip') implies a supported end. Which edge is restrained, and whether all of its nodes or only some are fixed, is shown only in Fig. 1a.
readings: entire edge opposite the loaded tip restrained (e.g., all 41 nodes at x = 0, load at mid-node of x = L)
mirror: entire right edge restrained, load at the mid-node of the left edge (a given angle theta then corresponds to pi - theta)
only part of that edge restrained (e.g., a central segment or the two end nodes)

items.entity: restraint on the supported edge
items.description: The text never says which degrees of freedom are fixed at the support. 'Cantilever' (Fig. 1 caption) suggests a clamped end but does not say so.
readings: fully clamped: ux = uy = 0 at every node of the support edge
ux = 0 on all edge nodes plus uy = 0 at a single node (roller-type support)

items.entity: definition of the load angle theta in [0, pi]
items.description: Sec. 5.2 and the Fig. 1 caption give the angle as uniform in [0, pi] (p(s) = 1/pi). They do not give the reference axis or the direction of rotation; load directions appear only as arrows in figures.
readings: theta counter-clockwise from +x pointing from the support toward the tip: 0 = axial tension, pi/2 = transverse upward, pi = axial compression
theta clockwise from +x (downward half-plane; mirror image of the first reading, same compliance)
theta measured from -x (toward the support): a given theta equals pi - theta of the first reading
theta measured from the -y axis, so [0, pi] spans the half-plane of loads with a positive axial (tension) component

items.entity: load angle(s) of the Case 1 sample solution(s) in Fig. 1a
items.description: The Fig. 1a caption gives no specific angle. Sec. 5.4 says four test loads (0.3pi, 0.4pi, 0.45pi, 0.55pi) are shown 'in Fig. 1' and marked in its 'last row', with compliance at the bottom. That description matches the Fig. 4 caption (rows a-d, ground truth in d), not Fig. 1, so the angle(s) actually used in Fig. 1a are not determined.
readings: unreported random draw(s) from U[0, pi]

items.entity: point load at the tip mid-node
items.description: No magnitude is given. Sec. 5.2 says the generator input is the load angle, while Sec. 5.3 says it is the x- and y-components of the load. Either way a fixed magnitude is implied, but its value is never stated.

items.entity: threshold alpha (global volume fraction and local density limit)
items.description: alpha appears in g0 and g1 of (TO)/(P) and in the initial guess x = alpha*1 (Alg. 2), but no value is given for Case 1 or anywhere else. Per Sec. 3.2 the same alpha bounds both the global mean density and the p-norm (p = 16) of the local average density.

items.entity: effective material volume of the reference (ground-truth) designs
items.description: Sec. 5.4 ('Validity of hyper-parameter settings') says ground-truth designs violate g0 by a mean of 4.89% in Case 1 (averaged over violating cases only) because of the AL tolerances. It does not say whether this is an absolute or relative excess, or whether a re-run should enforce g0 <= 0 exactly.
readings: absolute excess of about 0.049 (mean density ~ alpha + 0.049)

items.entity: density filter radius r_e (Eqs. 3-4)
items.description: The filter radius r_e is used in Eq. (4) and listed as an input to Alg. 2, but no value or unit is given.

items.entity: local-density averaging radius R_e (constraint g1)
items.description: Sec. 3.2 defines the local average density over a neighbourhood of radius R_e and notes that R_e differs from r_e. It is listed as an input to Alg. 2, but no value is given (only p = 16 is).

items.entity: neighbourhood N_e used for the local average density
items.description: Sec. 3.2 writes N_e = {i : ||x_i - x_e||_2 <= R_e}, using the design variables x, while element coordinates are written z in Eq. (4). A spatial distance is presumably meant.
readings: Euclidean distance between element centroids ||z_i - z_e|| <= R_e (circular neighbourhood)
literal reading: distance between design-variable values x_i and x_e

items.entity: Heaviside projection sharpness beta (Eq. 2) and continuation limit beta_t
items.description: Alg. 2 takes the initial beta and beta_t as inputs and doubles beta while beta < beta_t, but neither value is given. The beta at which final designs and their compliance are evaluated is also not stated.

items.entity: Young's modulus of solid material and out-of-plane thickness
items.description: Sec. 3.2 only says 'linear elastic material'. No modulus or thickness is given.

items.entity: Poisson's ratio
items.description: Poisson's ratio is not given anywhere.

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption
items.description: The text says only 'a 2D structure'; plane stress versus plane strain is not stated.

items.entity: density-to-stiffness interpolation (penalty exponent)
items.description: Sec. 3.2 only says K is 'established through the density vector rho'. No SIMP or RAMP law or penalty exponent is given (the p = 16 in the text is the p-norm exponent, not a penalty).
readings: SIMP, penalty 1 (no penalization; rely on Heaviside projection)

items.entity: minimum (void) stiffness
items.description: No lower bound on stiffness or density for void elements is given (needed to keep K nonsingular).

items.entity: optimizer and convergence criteria (Appendix Alg. 2, augmented Lagrangian)
items.description: Alg. 2 is incomplete or inconsistent in several places. The line-search 'while 1' loop has no exit after a step is accepted. eps_opt = 1e-3 is set but never used. Line 10 uses (mu + 2g/r)*grad g with an active-set switch, while L in lines 15-16 is mu*g + 0.5*g^2/r with no switch. The tolerances eps = eps_al = 1 on max|dx| are absolute, so they depend on the unstated load and E scale. There is no iteration cap. The Appendix also says MMA could be used instead.
readings: Alg. 2 as written, leaving the line search after the first accepted step, tolerances eps = eps_al = 1
AL with consistent gradient (mu + g/r)*grad g, same tolerances, plus an iteration cap
MMA with g0 and g1 as constraints and a standard tolerance (e.g., max design change <= 0.01)
